title: Trainspotting (film)
wiki_lead:
Trainspotting is a 1996 British independent black comedy drama film directed by Danny Boyle, with Ewan McGregor, Ewen Bremner, Jonny Lee Miller, Kevin McKidd, Robert Carlyle and Kelly Macdonald in her film debut. It is written in English and Scots. Based on the 1993 novel by Irvine Welsh and inspired by the stage production of the same name, the film was released in the United Kingdom on 23 February 1996.
The film follows a group of heroin addicts in an economically depressed area of Edinburgh, led by a mentally ill and violent psychopathic narcissist who allows their life of crime, and their passage through life. Themes in the film include drug addiction and urban poverty and squalor in Edinburgh.
Trainspotting was released to critical acclaim and is regarded by many critics as one of the best films of the 1990s. The film was ranked tenth by the British Film Institute (BFI) in its list of Top 100 British films of the 20th century. In 2004, the film was voted the best Scottish film of all time in a general public poll. A 2017 poll of 150 actors, directors, writers, producers and critics for Time Out ranked it the tenth best British film ever. A sequel, T2 Trainspotting, was released in January 2017 by Sony Pictures Releasing through its TriStar Pictures label.

Plot
Mark Renton, a 26-year-old unemployed heroin addict living with his parents in Leith, regularly takes drugs with his friends: treacherous, womanising James Bond fanatic Simon "Sick Boy" Williamson, and docile and bumbling Daniel "Spud" Murphy. Renton's other friends include aggressive alcoholic psychopath Francis "Franco" Begbie, who serves as the de facto leader of the group, and honest footballer Thomas "Tommy" Mackenzie, who both abstain from heroin use. 
Tiring of his reckless lifestyle, Renton attempts to wean himself off heroin with a bare room, food, and opium suppositories from dodgy dealer Mikey Forrester. Developing diarrhoea, he has to relieve himself in the disgusting toilet of a betting shop, then imagines swimming in the filthy water as he retrieves the suppositories.
On a night out, Renton notices that his cessation of heroin use has increased his libido. He seduces Diane Coulston, returning to her home to have sex. The following morning, he is horrified to learn that she is underage and lives with her parents, whom Renton mistakes for her flatmates. Diane threatens to report him to the police if he does not continue the relationship.
After several unsuccessful attempts to reintegrate into society, Renton, Sick Boy, and Spud relapse into heroin use; Tommy also begins to join them after Lizzy dumps him due to their sex tape disappearing (which Renton had stolen). Despite the group's shock at the negligence-induced death of Dawn, the infant daughter of Sick Boy and fellow heroin user Allison, they still do not quit using. When Renton, Sick Boy, and Spud engage in shoplifting, Renton and Spud are caught while Sick Boy narrowly escapes.

grok_lead: Trainspotting is a 1996 British black comedy-drama film directed by Danny Boyle in his second feature-length project, adapted from Irvine Welsh's 1993 novel of the same name by screenwriter John Hodge. The story follows the lives of a group of young heroin addicts in the economically deprived Leith area of Edinburgh, Scotland, centered on protagonist Mark "Renton" Renton ( Ewan McGregor) and his associates as they navigate cycles of addiction, crime, and attempts at withdrawal amid urban squalor. Starring McGregor alongside Ewen Bremner, Jonny Lee Miller, Kevin McKidd, and Robert Carlyle, the film employs a nonlinear narrative, visceral visuals, and a soundtrack featuring Britpop and electronic music to depict the highs and devastating lows of opioid dependence. Released on 23 February 1996 in the United Kingdom, Trainspotting grossed approximately $71.5 million worldwide against a budget of around Â£1.5 million (equivalent to about $3 million USD at the time), marking a significant commercial success and breakthrough for Boyle and McGregor. It garnered critical acclaim for its innovative direction, raw authenticity, and unflinching portrayal of addiction's consequences, including overdose, infant death, and social decay, earning a 90% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes from contemporary reviews and an 8.1/10 average user score on IMDb from over 750,000 ratings. The film secured 23 awards and 35 nominations, including an Academy Award nomination for Best Adapted Screenplay, BAFTA wins for Best British Film, Best Adapted Screenplay, and Best Editing, and recognition from the British Independent Film Awards. While celebrated as a cultural milestone that revitalized British cinema in the 1990s and influenced depictions of youth subcultures, Trainspotting sparked debate over its stylistic energyâsuch as hallucinatory sequences and Renton's defiant voiceover âpotentially glamorizing drug use despite explicit scenes of horror like violent withdrawal and HIV-related deaths. Critics and author Welsh noted that the film's rhythmic, unsparing realism countered government anti-drug campaigns by highlighting heroin 's destructive toll without moralizing, though some contemporaries accused it of aestheticizing addiction amid Scotland's real 1980s- 1990s heroin epidemic. This tension underscores its defining characteristic as a provocative examination of personal agency in the face of chemical dependency and socioeconomic despair, eschewing didacticism for causal directness in showing addiction 's inexorable pull and fallout.
